questiontext.text:
Here is some simple data giving the yield for {@number_rows@} different farms across different crop and fertiliser varieties.


You should complete the frequency table below and then determine whether the data is balanced or unbalanced.

Variety 1 Variety 2 Variety 3 Total
Fertiliser 1 [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]]
Fertiliser 2 [[input:ans5]] [[validation:ans5]] [[input:ans6]] [[validation:ans6]] [[input:ans7]] [[validation:ans7]] [[input:ans8]] [[validation:ans8]]
Fertiliser 3 [[input:ans9]] [[validation:ans9]] [[input:ans10]] [[validation:ans10]] [[input:ans11]] [[validation:ans11]] [[input:ans12]] [[validation:ans12]]
Total [[input:ans13]] [[validation:ans13]] [[input:ans14]] [[validation:ans14]] [[input:ans15]] [[validation:ans15]] {@number_rows@}

[[feedback:prt1]]

Is the data balanced?   [[input:ans16]] [[validation:ans16]]

[[feedback:prt2]]

prtcorrect.text: Correct answer, well done.

prtpartiallycorrect.text: Your answer is partially correct.

prtincorrect.text: Incorrect answer.

truefeedback.text:
All of the values in your table relating to a particular pairing of variety and fertiliser are correct.
However, check that you have correctly summed up the totals in each row and column!

falsefeedback.text:
Not all of the values in your table relating to a particular pairing of variety and fertiliser are correct.
Double check the data and ensure that you only count the farms which have planted the specified variety and fertiliser.

truefeedback.text:
[[ if test="is_balanced"]]

Good! All of the entries to the table are the same, so there is a balanced spread of data across all pairings of variety and fertiliser.

[[ else ]]

Good! There are differences between the different entries in the table, so there is not a balanced spread of data across all pairings of variety and fertiliser.

[[/ if ]]

falsefeedback.text:
[[ if test="is_balanced"]]

Not quite! All of the entries to the table are the same so there is balance in the data.
So, there is a balanced spread of data across all pairings of variety and fertiliser.

[[ else ]]

Not quite! There are differences between the different entries in the table. We have a largest entry of {@last(sort(table_data))@} compared to a smallest entry of {@first(sort(table_data))@}.
So, there is not a balanced spread of data across all pairings of variety and fertiliser.

[[/ if ]]
